metadata.title: fix: accept camelCase passthroughHeaders in gateway creation
metadata.author: abhin1899

description:
Closes #3577

## 📌 Summary
Fixes inconsistent API behavior where `passthroughHeaders` (camelCase) works in UPDATE but not CREATE operations.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
See issue #3577

## 🐞 Root Cause
`GatewayCreate` was extending `BaseModel` without automatic camelCase alias generation, while `GatewayUpdate` extends `BaseModelWithConfigDict` which includes `alias_generator=to_camel_case`.

## 💡 Fix Description
Changed `GatewayCreate` to extend `BaseModelWithConfigDict` (same as `GatewayUpdate`), ensuring:
- Automatic camelCase aliases for all snake_case fields
- Consistent behavior between CREATE and UPDATE operations
- Backward compatibility maintained (both naming conventions work)
- Proper serialization to camelCase in API responses

**Changes:**
- `mcpgateway/schemas.py`: Changed base class from `BaseModel` to `BaseModelWithConfigDict`
- Simplified `model_config` to only include `str_strip_whitespace=True`

## 🧪 Verification

| Check | Command | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Lint suite (`make lint`) | ✅ |
| Unit tests (`make test`) | ✅ |
| Manual testing | ✅ |

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted
- [x] DCO sign-off included
- [x] No secrets committed

**Test Results:**
```python
# camelCase (the bug we fixed)
GatewayCreate(passthroughHeaders=['billingId']) 
# ✅ Works now!

# snake_case (backward compatibility)
GatewayCreate(passthrough_headers=['billingId'])
# ✅ Still works!

# Serialization
gw.model_dump(by_alias=True)
# ✅ Outputs: {"passthroughHeaders": [...]}

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
✅ Overall Assessment: APPROVED with minor suggestions

   The fix correctly addresses the inconsistency between GatewayCreate and GatewayUpdate by making both extend BaseModelWithConfigDict.

   ---

   🔍 Code Changes Review

   ✅ Core Fix (mcpgateway/schemas.py:2541)
    1 -class GatewayCreate(BaseModel):
    2 +class GatewayCreate(BaseModelWithConfigDict):

   Strengths:
    - ✅ Minimal, surgical change
    - ✅ Achieves consistency with GatewayUpdate (line 2898)
    - ✅ Leverages existing BaseModelWithConfigDict infrastructure
    - ✅ Automatic camelCase alias generation via alias_generator=to_camel_case
    - ✅ Maintains backward compatibility (populate_by_name=True allows both naming conventions)

   Verification:
    - BaseModelWithConfigDict provides:
      - alias_generator=to_camel_case - converts snake_case → camelCase
      - populate_by_name=True - accepts both snake_case and camelCase input
      - from_attributes=True - ORM compatibility
      - use_enum_values=True - proper enum serialization

   ---

   🧪 Testing Observations

   Missing Test Coverage
   ⚠️ RECOMMENDATION: Add explicit test for this fix

   The codebase has extensive GatewayCreate tests (113 matches found), but none specifically test camelCase field acceptance. Consider adding:

```bash
# tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_schemas.py
def test_gateway_create_accepts_camelcase_passthrough_headers():
    """Test GatewayCreate accepts camelCase passthroughHeaders (issue #3577)."""
     # camelCase input
     gw = GatewayCreate(
          name="test",
          url="http://example.com",
           passthroughHeaders=["X-Custom", "X-Trace"]
     )
     assert gw.passthrough_headers == ["X-Custom", "X-Trace"]
    
     # Verify serialization
     serialized = gw.model_dump(by_alias=True)
     assert "passthroughHeaders" in serialized
     assert serialized["passthroughHeaders"] == ["X-Custom", "X-Trace"]
    
def test_gateway_create_backward_compatible_snake_case():
    """Test GatewayCreate still accepts snake_case (backward compatibility)."""
    gw = GatewayCreate(
        name="test",
        url="http://example.com",
        passthrough_headers=["X-Custom"]
     )
    assert gw.passthrough_headers == ["X-Custom"]
```
   ---

   📋 Additional Considerations

   1. Model Config Override
   The model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True) on line 2562 correctly overrides only the str_strip_whitespace setting while inheriting all other config from BaseModelWithConfigDict.

   ✅ This is the right approach - it doesn't break the inherited alias_generator.

   2. Consistency Check
   Both schemas now use the same base class:
    - GatewayCreate(BaseModelWithConfigDict) ✅
    - GatewayUpdate(BaseModelWithConfigDict) ✅

   3. API Response Behavior
   FastAPI automatically uses by_alias=True when serializing responses, so all API responses will now correctly use camelCase field names for GatewayCreate responses.

   4. Impact on Other Fields
   This change affects ALL snake_case fields in `GatewayCreate`, not just `passthrough_headers`:
    - passthrough_headers → passthroughHeaders
    - auth_type → authType
    - auth_username → authUsername
    - auth_password → authPassword
    - auth_token → authToken
    - auth_header_key → authHeaderKey
    - auth_header_value → authHeaderValue
    - auth_headers → authHeaders
    - oauth_config → oauthConfig
    - auth_query_param_key → authQueryParamKey
    - auth_query_param_value → authQueryParamValue
    - auth_value → authValue
    - one_time_auth → oneTimeAuth
    - team_id → teamId
    - owner_email → ownerEmail
    - ca_certificate → caCertificate
    - ca_certificate_sig → caCertificateSig
    - signing_algorithm → signingAlgorithm
    - refresh_interval_seconds → refreshIntervalSeconds
    - gateway_mode → gatewayMode

   This is actually GOOD - it makes the entire API consistent with MCP specification's camelCase convention.

   ---

   🎯 Recommendations

   High Priority
    1. ✅ Merge as-is - The fix is correct and minimal
    2. ⚠️ Add regression test - Prevent future regressions of this specific issue

   Low Priority (Future Enhancements)
    3. 📝 Consider documenting the camelCase/snake_case dual-input behavior in API docs
    4. 🔍 Audit other schema classes for similar inconsistencies (though this appears to be the only one)

   ---

   ✅ Final Verdict

   APPROVED - This is a well-targeted fix that:
    - Solves the reported issue (#3577)
    - Maintains backward compatibility
    - Improves API consistency
    - Follows existing patterns in the codebase
    - Has minimal risk

   The only improvement would be adding an explicit regression test for this specific scenario.

LGTM 🚀
